main_body: Repeating stone-brick surface pattern filling the whole tile area (terrain/wall face), no standing object
top_band: none - flat seamless terrain pattern, no standing volume; a single column crosses alternating brick faces and dark mortar rows
evidence: The candidate is a terrain tile (stone brick paving or wall face), not a standing object, so the top-band and front-face contract does not apply. The bricks have lighter upper edges and dark mortar gaps that give a slight relief. There are no receding side faces and no object volume to fail.

style.evidence: The bricks use about five steps: a deep mortar tone, dark, mid, light and a highlight on the top edge of the lighter bricks. The mortar and outlines are a dark brown-grey that leans toward the stone, not neutral black. Individual bricks carry highlight dots, edge shading and a few darker speckles, comparable to the reference paving. The darker brick rows have some quieter, flatter areas, so density is slightly under the richest reference tiles. Overall it would sit acceptably next to the reference.
